1.definition: The last attested emperor of the Gupta dynasty, who ruled around 540–550 CE over a much-reduced territory centered on Magadha in eastern India. After his reign, Gupta imperial inscriptions stop appearing entirely.

1.matchText: routes down the Ganges to Bengal

2.definition: The older sister of the north Indian king Harsha. Her marriage to the Maukhari king Grahavarman of Kannauj tied her family's Pushyabhuti dynasty to the Maukharis across the upper Ganges plain.

A minister who attempted to seize power in Kannauj after Harsha died without an heir in 647 CE. He attacked a Tang Chinese diplomatic mission passing through Magadha, prompting the Chinese envoy Wang Xuance to raise a Tibetan force that defeated and captured him.

A Sanskrit courtly romance attributed to the emperor Harsha, depicting the love between a king and a princess in disguise. It is one of three plays credited to Harsha's patronage and survives as one of the few examples of seventh-century Sanskrit dramatic composition from a reigning monarch's court.

8.definition: The short name for al-Biruni's eleventh-century study of India, fully titled "Book of Verifying What India Has." It's a detailed scholarly account of Indian science, religion, and customs by a visiting Muslim polymath.

A city in the ancient region of Khwarazm (modern Uzbekistan/Turkmenistan) where the polymath al-Biruni was born in 973 CE. Kath was the capital of Khwarazm before the city of Gurganj superseded it; al-Biruni's full name identifies him as the son of Kath.
